title: Ordered closed families and unit-normalized signed augmented row data
statement:
Let $X,Z$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $i:Z\to X$ a scheme morphism, and $A$ a sheaf of commutative rings on the small pro-etale site of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and the actual closed restriction functors $E_j$, units $\eta_j$, finite intersections, ordered terms $D_F^p$, signed differential matrices, and horizontal-first double complexes and totals of [def-sfb-finite-closed-row-constructions]. Use integer cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

An ordered closed family over $i$ is a positive finite length $m$, objects $F_a\to X$ of schemes over $X$, closed immersions $F_a\to X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], a nonempty set of factorizations of each through $i$, and quasi-compact complementary open immersions in $X$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. There is no covering condition.

A signed row for such a family consists of the following specified data and equations (this is a structure, not an existence assertion). Each $E_i$ and $E_{F_s}$ is additive. There are natural transformations $r_{s,t}:E_{F_s}\to E_{F_t}$ for all pairs of subsets, with $\eta_{F_s}r_{s,t}=\eta_{F_t}$ whenever $s\subseteq t$ and $r_{s,t}r_{t,h}=r_{s,h}$ for $s\subseteq t\subseteq h$. For every nonempty $s$ there is $r_{Z,s}:E_i\to E_{F_s}$ satisfying $\eta_i r_{Z,s}=\eta_{F_s}$ and $r_{Z,s}r_{s,t}=r_{Z,t}$ for nonempty $s\subseteq t$. There is an additive row functor $R$ from module sheaves to integer cochain complexes and natural term isomorphisms $R^p\simeq D_F^p$ for every natural $p$, identifying its differential with the given signed matrix. Its terms are zero for integer $p<0$ or $p\geq m$. The augmentation $a:E_i\to R^0$ has singleton components exactly $r_{Z,\{a\}}$. It is the degree-zero part of a specified chain augmentation $\alpha:E_i[0]\to R$, with degree-zero component the canonical single-object identification followed by $a$. Finally there is a natural total augmentation from $E_i$ applied termwise to $K$ into $\operatorname{Tot}_R(K)$, whose degree-$n$ component is $a_{K^n}$ followed by the $(0,n)$ diagonal coproduct inclusion. No data are chosen from an existence theorem.
